shiftNote: Anchored to a 7:00 AM shift with recording from 8:00 AM. Other shifts keep the same sequence.

day.text: The anchors open the device room, count the phones, check every battery, login, and upload, and hand each phone to its wearer.
Thirty-minute cycles until 4:00 PM. The wearer works the task, and the anchor restarts every cycle.
At every reset the anchor looks at what was just recorded and fixes problems on the spot.
Every phone comes back by device number, is inspected, counted, and docked to charge.

The Portfolio Manager goes through everything the site recorded today, pulls anything that should not go out, and sends the day's report to Mano by 6:00 PM: hours, active phones, hardware, problems, and fixes.
Anyone who cannot make tomorrow's shift has called and messaged their Portfolio Manager by now.

day.what: The hub run and the upload
day.text: The phones go to the closest hub a third at a time and upload over fiber overnight.
Two reviewers on the quality control team watch every video. If either says delete, it is deleted.

week.note: Client update. Adham sends it; Mano supplies the numbers.
Full flush of every device before the day off. Factory phones to a hub.
Day off in Egypt. Hotels only, on their own lines.

weekly: Book review: each Portfolio Manager against target, once a week.
Registry count: once a week, on the same day, the registry, the MDM, and the device room are counted against each other at every site and hub. Any variance is investigated the same day.

month.text: Beat last month and the book grows. Miss twice and it shrinks.
Youssef Medhat runs the audit passes. Flagged footage is deleted.
The invoice goes out on accepted hours only.
Payroll, site payments, referral and performance bonuses through Mano.

items: Thursday: full flush of every device before the Friday day off, and a Friday plan for sites that keep running
Sunday: Adham sends the client update; Mano supplies the numbers
Book review: each Portfolio Manager against target
Books re-earned: beat it and it grows, miss twice and it shrinks
Month-end audit passes by Youssef Medhat before the invoice goes out
Payroll, site payments, referral and performance bonuses through Mano
Absences by 8 PM the night before, or it counts as a no-show
One account per person, never shared, never recycled
Three flags pulls a worker; a second strike pauses the device
Nobody names the client, to anyone, for any reason

phases.title: Morning: the phones go out
phases.note: Clock-in is 7:00 AM, and the anchors, one per ten phones, take the phones out of the device room.

phases.title: During the shift
phases.note: Recording runs from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM in 30-minute cycles, and the anchor checks the footage at every reset.

phases.title: Shift end: the phones come back
phases.note: The shift ends at 4:00 PM, every phone comes back, and the Portfolio Manager reviews the day before anything uploads.

phases.title: Night: the hub run
phases.note: The phones go to the closest hub a third at a time, upload over fiber, and two reviewers watch every video.

phases.title: Before the next shift
phases.note: The phones come back cleared and charged before the anchors clock in.

steps.title: Open the device room
steps.done: The room is open at 7:00 AM and every phone is still on its charger from the morning return.
lines: Open the device room at 7:00 AM. This is the pickup location: the phones live here, on their chargers, and nowhere else.
Hold the key yourself. Nobody from the site opens this room, and nobody takes a phone off a charger before the count.
Call the anchors in. There is one anchor for every ten phones. Wearers wait at the pickup point outside the room until their name is called.
The first cycle starts at 8:00 AM, so the hour between is for the checks below. Be early.

steps.title: Count the phones, log the number
steps.done: The number you wrote on the count sheet is the number the site should have. If it is not, the Portfolio Manager already knows.
lines: Count every phone on the chargers. Count the spares too.
Write the number on the count sheet with the time and your name. The sheet stays in the device room.
Check the number against the manifest that came back with the runner this morning. Same number, or something is missing.
A phone missing at 7:00 AM goes to the Portfolio Manager now, not at the end of the shift. If nobody can find it, lost mode starts within the hour.

steps.title: Check every battery and login
steps.done: Every phone is charged, the collection app is open, and every phone is on its wearer's own account.
lines: Pick up each phone and read the battery. A phone that did not charge goes back on the charger, and a spare takes its place today.
Open the collection app on each phone. Confirm the account on it belongs to the wearer who will carry it today, in their own name.
Never let a wearer log into someone else's account, not for one cycle. A shared account puts someone else's fraud on their name.
A phone on the wrong account, or a login that will not work, goes to the Portfolio Manager before it goes on anyone's head.

steps.title: Check last night's upload finished
steps.done: Every phone shows zero pending uploads in the collection app.
lines: Open the collection app on each phone and look at pending uploads. The number must be zero.
The hub attendant checked this on the dashboard before the phones left the hub. Check it again here anyway.
A phone still holding yesterday's footage does not go on a head. Put it aside and tell the Portfolio Manager the same hour.
Footage on a phone at clock-in is backlog. The Portfolio Manager counts it in device-days, and a site holding more than one device-day is an incident that Moharam hears about the same day.

steps.title: Hand each phone to its wearer
steps.done: Every phone out of the room has a row in the wearer log with a name and a device number.
lines: Call the wearer by name. Only a wearer who passed onboarding screening gets a phone: ID copy on file, consent signed, fraud briefing signed off, one account in their own name. No file, no phone, no matter who at the site sent them.
Hand over the phone by device number. Write the row in the wearer log: name, device number, site, date.
Hand over the cap and the mount with it. Every wearer gets their own rig.
A wearer who looks under 18 or has no ID gets no phone. Tell the Portfolio Manager now.

steps.title: Fit the rig, set the angle
steps.done: Every wearer is standing with the cap on, the mount tight, and the camera seeing what their eyes see.
lines: Cap on. Mount tight. Phone seated so it cannot slip. On a site that needs a helmet, the mount goes on the certified helmet without changing it.
Set the angle: first person, hands and the work in the frame. Not the torso, not the floor, not a chest strap. A chest mount is fraud in the client's system, comfortable or not.
Say it again while you fit it: hat off means tap stop. First the button, then the hat.
Check the wearer has the site's safety gear on before they walk to the floor. Missing PPE means they do not film until it is on.
On elevated work, tether the phone. A phone falling from height is an incident.

steps.title: Start the first cycle at 8:00
steps.who: The wearer, watched by the anchor
steps.done: Every phone on the floor is recording by 8:00 AM with a clean angle.
lines: At 8:00 AM the wearer taps start and begins the assigned task. Not before. The hour from 7:00 is for the checks.
Walk the floor in the first minutes. Look at each phone: recording running, angle right, the wearer working.
While the cycle runs the wearer works the task without stopping. No personal phone, no calls, no chatting, no breaks on camera.
A wearer with no work to do taps stop, tells you, and takes the rig off. Idle footage is fraud.

steps.title: Reset and check every 30 minutes
steps.done: Every phone restarted on time, and what was just recorded looked right before the next cycle began.
lines: The buzz at the end of the cycle is the cue. Restart every phone per the procedure, and sweep the floor as the backup for every restart.
At every reset look at what was just recorded: the angle, the lighting, the wearer still working. Fix problems on the spot: refit the rig, reset the angle, remind the wearer.
Read storage and battery on each phone at the same time. A storage warning means a spare goes in now and that phone is flushed first tonight.
A wearer who will not follow the cycle comes off the phone. Tell the Portfolio Manager. Not following the rules during a cycle means removal from the site.
Ten phones is what one anchor can sweep every 30 minutes. Past ten, restarts slip and flags climb.

steps.title: The Portfolio Manager drops in
steps.done: The site has been seen today at a time nobody expected, and the wrap report will say what was found.
lines: Come unannounced, at a different time each day. Two or three visits a day in the first week after launch, one or two in the second, and at least once a day after that.
Check the camera angles, the 30-minute cycle, the chargers, custody in the wearer log, and how the wearers are doing.
Read every flag the same day it arrives. Take it to the worker on the floor within 24 hours, with the video open and one specific correction. Watch their next cycle for the fix.
What you found and what you fixed goes in the wrap report tonight.

steps.title: A phone fails mid-shift
steps.who: The anchor first, then the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: The wearer is recording again on a spare, on their own account, and the swap is written down.
lines: Tap stop. Take the rig off the wearer's head. Do not let a wearer keep working with a phone that is not recording. Those minutes are gone either way.
Check the easy things first: app open, wearer on their own account, recording running, battery, storage.
If it is the phone, swap in a spare the same minute. The wearer logs into their own account on the spare and the cycle restarts. The site never waits for a repair.
Write the swap in the wearer log and tell the Portfolio Manager: device number, what broke, whether footage is still on it. Every transfer is a registry event the same day.

The failed phone goes back to the device room with its footage still on it. If it can still upload, it rides to the hub tonight. Repairs batch weekly to one shop, and if the same part keeps failing across phones, Ali hears with photos and a count.

steps.title: Collect every phone at shift end
steps.done: Every phone issued this morning is back in the anchor's hands, by device number, against the wearer log.
lines: The last cycle ends at 4:00 PM. The wearer taps stop first, then takes the hat off, and brings the whole rig to the anchor.
Take each phone back by device number and tick the wearer's row in the wearer log. Cap and mount come back with it.
Count the rigs as they come in against the morning's rows.
A phone not returned goes to the Portfolio Manager before anyone goes home. A phone anywhere but the site, a hub, or a signed-for case is a missing phone, and lost mode starts within the hour.

steps.title: Inspect and count again
steps.who: The anchors, checked by the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: Every phone has a condition tick and the evening count matches the morning count.
lines: Tick the condition on every phone: screen, port, mount, battery. Write it against the device number.
A cracked screen, a bad port, or a loose mount means a spare goes in for tomorrow and the damaged phone is logged for the weekly repair batch.
Count the phones again and write the number on the count sheet, with the time and your name. It must match the morning number.
The Portfolio Manager checks the count and the ticks before clocking out. A number that does not match is the Portfolio Manager's problem tonight, not tomorrow.

steps.title: Dock to charge, check storage
steps.done: Every phone is on a charger in the device room and every storage warning is marked for tonight's manifest.
lines: Dock every phone on a charger in the device room. The kit gives two multi-port chargers and a power strip per ten phones. Lay the cables so nobody trips.
Read storage on every phone as you dock it. Any phone with a storage warning is marked to be flushed first at the hub tonight.
Lock the room. The phones stay here until the Portfolio Manager has reviewed the day and the runner arrives.
Nothing sleeps holding more than a day of footage. At a hub site the upload happens at the hub, not here, which is why the run cannot slip.

steps.title: Portfolio Manager reviews the day
steps.done: Everything the site recorded today has been looked at, anything that should not go out is pulled, and the wrap report is with Mano by 6:00 PM.
lines: At 5:00 PM go through everything the site recorded today, phone by phone, before any of it uploads. This is the second quality layer. The anchor's check at each reset was the first.
Pull anything that should not go out: a restroom, a screen, an ID document, a person under 18, a rig on a chest. Note the session, the device number, and the wearer.
Send the wrap report to Mano by 6:00 PM: hours, active phones, hardware status, problems, fixes worth copying, backlog in device-days, and the day's wearer log rows.
Then release the phones to the runner. No phone leaves for the hub before this review is done.

steps.title: Pack a third per run
steps.who: The anchors, the runner, and the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: The runner has signed for one case, and the manifest inside names every phone in it.
lines: Never put more than a third of the site's phones in one case, one vehicle, or one run. Thirty phones means three runs of ten. Above 60 phones, two runners on staggered runs.
Use a locked, unmarked hard case. Put the printed manifest inside: device IDs, count, site, time out, runner name. Mark the phones to be flushed first.
The runner counts the phones against the manifest before signing. Count before you sign. No signature, no handover.

The Portfolio Manager signs the phones out to the runner, or the senior anchor signs if the Portfolio Manager has left. Both signatures are custody at pickup. MDM location tracking is on for every phone in the case.
The first run leaves as soon as the Portfolio Manager's review is done. The last run is at the hub before 11 PM.

steps.title: Drive straight to the closest hub
steps.done: Every case is at the hub and signed for, and the runner never stopped between the site and the hub.
lines: Take the case to the hub closest to the site: the central hub downtown, Sheikh Zayed, or the Fifth Settlement. The site plan says which.
Carry the letter kit in the bag: the Arabic company letter on letterhead, a copy of the commercial register, the device list, and two phone numbers that answer.
Never stop en route. Never take phones home. Phones live at the site, at a hub, or in a signed-for case, nowhere else.
At a checkpoint, hand over the letter, the register, and the manifest, and call Moharam. Never argue, never hide the count.
Go back for the next third. No runs after 11 PM, so the first run has to leave early enough for the last one to make it.

steps.title: Hub intake: count, sign, dock
steps.done: Every phone on the manifest is counted, signed for, on a charger, and uploading.
lines: Receive each case against its manifest. Count the phones. Both of you sign. That is custody at the drop end.
Dock every phone on charge and confirm the collection app is uploading over the hub's fiber. Phones marked to be flushed first go on first.
A phone that will not upload is held, and the hold goes in the log.
Log the night: TB moved, devices cleared, devices held. Two nights over 70% of hub capacity triggers the next-hub search.
If the hub's line goes down, call Mano. Moharam sends the remaining runs to the second hub the same hour.

steps.title: Upload overnight, confirm on the dashboard
steps.who: The hub attendant, then two reviewers on the quality control team
steps.done: Every phone going back shows completed uploads on the dashboard, and every video has two reviewers' verdicts.
lines: The phones upload over the hub's fiber through the night. An hour of footage is 5.4 GB, so a site's day takes hours, and that is why the phones cannot wait for the morning.
Before any phone is released, confirm on the dashboard that its uploads completed. A phone leaves the hub empty or it does not leave.
Charge every phone while it uploads. Repack per site with a new manifest: device IDs, count, site, time out, runner name.

After the upload, two reviewers on the quality control team watch every video. If either one says delete, it is deleted. It counts only when both accept it. Flags reach the Portfolio Manager the same day.

steps.title: Back on the chargers before 7:00
steps.who: The runner, received by the senior anchor
steps.done: Every cleared phone is on its charger in the device room, signed for, before the anchors clock in at 7:00 AM.
lines: Take back only phones the hub has cleared, with the new manifest inside each case. Count against it before you sign at the hub.
Same rules on the way back: a third per run, a locked unmarked case, the letter in the bag, never stop, MDM tracking on.
At the site, the person who opens the device room counts the phones against the manifest, and both of you sign custody at the drop. Put every phone on a charger.
A phone the hub held does not come back. It shows on the dashboard, and the Portfolio Manager puts a spare on that wearer's head today.
The runner is done before 7:00 AM. The anchors never wait for the phones.

steps.title: The morning after
steps.who: The anchors, then the Portfolio Manager
steps.done: At 7:00 AM the count, the batteries, the logins, and last night's upload are checked again, and the day starts over.
lines: At 7:00 AM it starts again: open the room, count the phones, write the number, check every battery and every login, and check that last night's upload finished.

Every flag from last night's review reaches the wearer within 24 hours, on the floor, with the video open. Three flags pulls the worker. A second strike pauses the phone until the worker is retrained.
